Immediate VIC horizontal expansion bitmask for field sprites.
Immediate sprite multicolour mask patched from the type-specific actor table.
Value written into the VIC sprite background priority register during field setup.
Frames remaining for the alternating hit display. The flash logic forces sprite colours 5 and 6 to white and toggles the actor phase. On expiry clear both actor activation flags.

Merge object enables and high X bits into the VIC registers, update sprites 4–7 and install their four pointers in both field screens. The last tests can mask the upper three sprites or disable all sprites.
Single RTS byte immediately after the preceding routine's return, before the next entry at $8EB4.
Switch from the cave subsection to the train first. After the train or a later stage, clear the subsection flag and advance the main stage index. Reenter setup at $7DD6.
Count X down through an entire byte range, then decrement Y and repeat while its sign bit stays clear.
Convert the player's world X into six panel glyphs at $C351 and world Y into a second six-glyph field at $C379. The caller of this path remains open.
Queue sound effect 3, put the hit point 21 pixels to the left or right of Indy at his current Y, and call the actor hit test with a horizontal tolerance of 10 pixels.
Toggle the half-rate action clock and advance the pose at $7B7A every other call. At pose $17 clear the action. For pose $15 test for tile $10 beside Indy and use it to position the secondary sprite.
Replace the player's X coordinate with the two bytes saved at $909C before the temporary probe offset.
Low byte of the player coordinate saved before shifting the origin for the two tile probes at $9026 and $9031.
High byte of the player coordinate saved with the low byte at $909C.
Restore the temporary X position and build a secondary sprite origin at the player's height, offset horizontally according to facing. The pose index at $90D2 selects the sprite source.
Immediate index doubled to select a source pointer from $9104. After copying layer four, phases two and above defer the final sprite-bank switch through $8765.
Low halves of interleaved source addresses read at even offsets according to pose.
High halves of the interleaved addresses beginning at $9104. The selected pointer is passed to the layer copier at $90EC.
Play sound effect seven. Place the projectile 31 pixels left of Indy and 14 pixels above him, then add 38 to the X coordinate for the other facing. Save facing for the projectile and sprite copier.
A selects an eight-byte pattern at $CEE8. Copy each byte twice into $CF80, producing a vertically doubled 16-byte image.
Use A as the horizontal tolerance. Reject inactive actors, types two through six, and targets outside the saved coordinate window. A hit queues an effect, starts the flash delay and adds 15 points.
Maximum accepted horizontal magnitude is one less than this byte. The hit test also checks equal high coordinate bytes and a vertical magnitude below $1E before changing actor state.
Load the self-modified map animation index and advance it modulo four.
Modulo-four slot index stored in the immediate byte of $921B. At slot zero the code toggles the separate animation phase.
Immediate byte of the load at $9228. It toggles every fourth call to the updater and selects the two replacement tile codes used for the catacombs animation.
Dispatch stage zero to $9368. In the catacombs, schedule or update a four-cell tile animation using X as a slot index and $FE/$FF as the top-left cell pointer.
Clear two pairs of adjacent cells one map row apart. The phase decides whether to draw the next four-cell image, advance the pointer or clear the slot.
Second phase-dependent code patched into the four-cell catacombs tile animation.
Patched first tile code in the catacombs phase that writes the four-cell image with the $98/$99 pair in the lower row.
Four high bytes for map-animation slots. A zero high byte and zero low byte together mean the slot is awaiting a location.
Four low bytes of active map-animation locations. During the search this array also holds the remaining candidate-row count.
Four flags set after the second pair of tile codes is drawn. The next update clears the cells and frees that slot.
Two phase-dependent codes written below the anchor row.
Two corresponding codes for the adjacent cell on the same row.
Add $96 to the 16-bit pointer at $FE/$FF to select the same column on the next 150-cell row.
Subtract $96 from the 16-bit pointer at $FE/$FF to select the same column on the preceding row.
Two starting tile IDs used in alternate phases when drawing the moving caves shape.
Forward the caves animation path to the routine that restores the old cells and updates the replacement pair.
Immediate countdown or phase at $9375. A zero phase searches candidate map rows above Indy, then records a valid anchor and the original glyphs so the next phase can replace them.
Patch the animation's 16-bit location and save the original bytes from two consecutive map rows for restoration.
Saved high byte of the current two-row animation anchor.
Saved low part of the pointer used to restore the previous image.
Immediate first tile restored at the saved animation anchor.
Original tile code from the second row, used to restore the map before advancing the two-row animated image.
Read the tile at the supplied pointer and column. Return one for approved nonzero tile IDs below $97 with contact class one or three, and otherwise return zero.
Select the current slot from the four-phase updater and, on slot zero, advance the common shape frame before erasing and redrawing the selected stamp.
Toggle the frame and choose $E7 or $F0 from $9363 as the first tile of the shape. The phase variable at $7D2E picks the centre glyph to restore.
Immediate flag tested after the old map cells are restored. When enabled, examine a candidate row and retain or change the stored row direction.
Store the new pointer into the active slot, then draw eight consecutive tile codes into three map rows, skipping the first column of the last row.
First tile code used to write the moving shape. The remaining codes are formed by successive additions.
Restore blank cells and the saved centre glyph to the previous position. Preserve the original pointer high byte across the three-row loop.
Immediate tile to restore in the middle column when clearing the preceding position. The eraser also reads this operand for another cell in the bottom row.
Initial pointer low bytes for four moving map stamps.
Initial pointer high bytes paired with $954A to address four moving map stamps.
Per-slot row direction. The probe updates these flags when a candidate row lacks a blocking tile.
Centre glyph used when restoring a vacated map position.
Load the scripted action phase before toggling it. The action advances on alternate calls.
Toggle this immediate byte and step the current action on phase zero. The index selects horizontal and signed vertical motion and a secondary sprite pattern.
Horizontal step loaded at $95C1 and taken in the direction selected by player facing.
Low source byte for the restored object position. The special frame can shift the saved coordinate by $30.
High source byte for the restored object position, adjusted on carry or borrow from the frame-specific shift.
Clear the action counter, the action latch, the movement mode and the saved joystick.
Per-frame horizontal displacement magnitude for the scripted action.
Signed per-frame vertical displacement. Negative values call the upward movement routine with the magnitude, and nonnegative values call the downward routine.
Store the caller's column mask. Mix the two counters and use the result to add a masked column offset or subtract ten from the tile pointer.
Mask passed in A to $9601. Restrict the counter-derived column adjustment before adding it to the map pointer.
Masked low byte of the software seed used as the positive horizontal offset to the tile pointer.
Bank in the RAM beneath ROM and I/O with $01=$34. Select four component patterns through animation tables at $9696, $9702, $96CC and $9738. Copy or mirror each through $9C82, then restore $01=$35.
Low bytes of the interleaved player upper outline source pointers, paired with $9697.
High bytes of interleaved pointers indexed by twice the player pose. The matching low bytes begin at $9696.
Low bytes of the interleaved player lower outline source pointers, paired with $96CD.
High bytes paired with the low bytes at $96CC for the lower outline layer.
Low bytes of the interleaved player upper fill source pointers, paired with $9703.
High bytes paired with the low bytes at $9702 for the upper fill layer.
Low bytes of the interleaved player lower fill source pointers, paired with $9739.
High bytes paired with the low bytes at $9738 for the lower fill layer.
Set up the title-screen IRQ and VIC bank, convert the high score, copy six pages of title glyphs from $BB48 to $0800, draw the logo and start title music.
Synchronize with the IRQ, advance the attract-page timing and sample joystick port 2. Fire reaches the game-start path through $98C0.
Immediate timer decremented by $80. A borrow allows the title page countdown step.
Immediate index of the title page. The title loop alternates pages zero and one on timer expiry and uses page three for a separate fire and countdown path.
Flag patched from the stage table. It selects between the comparison-only countdown path and writing the glyph to $066B.
Immediate value of the current countdown glyph. Code writes it to the title screen until it reaches $6B or the player presses fire.
Immediate operand of the load at $98B9. The keyboard polling path clears it at $98C5 and restores the idle CIA1 row selection before the next title pass.
Enter the row-by-row title erase loop at $9901 when fire is detected.
Read successive CIA1 keyboard rows. When both comparisons at $98D0 and $98DC match, call $9C2F with Y=$0D and enable the room-selection scan through $7FD3.
Clear 21 rows of 40 title cells at one row per raster synchronization. Set border zero, reset the IRQ selection operand and silence the music driver.
Tick the driver except on the skipped timing slots, clear the foreground raster mailbox and keep the title IRQ on raster line zero.
Immediate countdown incremented under the timing-mode test in the title IRQ. On reaching five, reset it and skip the driver tick.
Four low bytes of text streams selected by the title page index.
Four high bytes paired with the screen text addresses at $998A.

Clear the message area, choose a stream using $9849 and consume its row records. Zero skips a row, a positive byte starts a row at that column and the following byte gives the colour. A negative row marker terminates the page and $FF ends a row's text.
Patched low address byte of the row-command read in the title printer.
Page byte of the indexed row-command fetch. It is patched with the selected page's text address.
Patched low address byte of the colour-command read in the title printer.
High byte of the indexed load that reads the colour command following the row's column byte.
Mask each message byte to six bits. Codes below $30 add $7C and codes from $30 add $3C, then write that glyph and the row colour to the output.
Low address byte patched from the chosen title-page text pointer.
High byte of the text stream's indexed load, paired with its low operand at $9A05.
Colour patched from the row record after the column byte and written alongside each translated character.
Twelve source bytes for the first subtitle row including its space padding. $980F converts it into the loaded title font's glyph numbers.
Source text for LAST CRUSADE. The title setup writes the converted glyphs at $0500.
Copyright, high-score digits and fire prompt in the row format that starts with column and colour, then text and a row terminator.
Six screen-text bytes updated after converting the saved high score. The containing text stream proceeds to the fire prompt.
First credits stream selected by the second entry of $998A/$998E. The row commands position and colour the programmer, graphics, music and coordination credits.
Attract-text stream containing the message that Indy has rescued his father.
Row records selected by the fourth entry of $998A/$998E, containing the lives and continue display.
First command byte of the continue-screen prompt record. Its printable text is PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE GAME.
Character bytes for the title’s cheat message, including the strings CHEAT MODE ON and FREAKY DANCING.
Copy 14 selected bytes backwards from the message table. Convert them to title glyphs and use colour four.
Select title page two, display it through the title routine and restore the page selection to zero on return.

Set continue-screen mode and countdown glyph. The stage flag selects a blank row before the fire prompt or terminates the page at that row. On the temple path reduce the saved stage index from three to two before re-entering the title display.
Stage-indexed flag copied into the countdown-mode operand at $9885. The indexed read includes the fourth byte at $9C81.
Fourth continue-screen stage flag, read at $9C61 for the temple. Stage initialization also writes this byte at $ADDB.

A selects a destination sprite layer, X and Y supply source address high and low. Patch the absolute load/store operands. Copy 64 bytes directly or use the reversal lookup and destination-byte permutation in the flipped path.
Low source address byte of the plain sprite copy, patched along with the corresponding mirrored source operand.
High byte of the direct source address patched from X by the shared sprite copier.
Low destination address byte of the plain sprite copy.
High byte of the direct sprite-copy store. It is patched from the selected layer pointer before a 64-byte reverse-indexed copy.
Low source address byte of the mirrored sprite copy.
High byte of the mirrored source address. The mirrored path reads exactly the same source record chosen by the calling layer updater.
Always patched to $E8 in the two mirror lookup paths. The high operand chooses which generated table the indexed load uses.
Patched to $06 for two-bit-pair reversal or $0E for bit-by-bit reversal. The lookup result is stored at a triplet-reversed byte position.
Low destination address byte of the mirrored sprite copy.
Patched high byte of the mirrored store destination. Its low byte and the sprite byte permutation determine the address within the selected layer buffer.
Destination offsets for reversing each left, middle and right byte triplet in a 21-row sprite. This is the index permutation used after the per-byte bit reversal.
Four little-endian sprite destinations for the first bank of working player layers. Indexed by twice the layer number when the bank flag is clear.
High bytes read at odd offsets in the first layer destination table at $9D4F.
Four little-endian sprite destinations used by the alternate working player layer buffer.
High bytes read at odd offsets in the second layer destination table at $9D5F.
Save facing and animation state, then route on the action-state byte at $7B9A. State zero probes the map around the player and tests for new joystick actions.
Probe map classifications around the player at offsets $0C/$16, $04/$16 and $14/$16. Class 3 in these probes applies damage ticks before continuing to the support test.
Probe map classification at offset $0C/$26. Class $0C sets $7AAF, class zero goes to the unsupported path, and class 3 calls $A2CF.
Horizontal scan correction derived from the high sprite X bit before the screen-cell column is calculated.
Screen column computed from the sprite coordinate and used as the stopping index in the $E0 tile scan.
Counter seeded with $FF and advanced for every $E0 tile encountered on the screen scan. A mismatch against the riddle's saved selection clears five cells in the map before room zero is initialized.
Set the action counter to $FF, set movement mode one and save joystick input. The following updates apply lateral steering and use a pose table to choose the vertical displacement.
Low three bits of Indy’s world Y, saved for the subtraction at $A09D. The code uses the remaining distance to align the landing to the tile grid.
Test saved horizontal direction bits, set facing and probe the leading edge at two or three heights. Move two pixels in that direction if all sampled cells differ from contact class one.
Reset the fall duration operand before starting the first falling update.
Increment the fall duration and probe below the player. Continue descending four pixels when unsupported, otherwise use time above 15 to calculate landing damage.
Immediate byte incremented by the falling path and cleared at entry or after the hard-landing damage calculation.
Duration-derived damage for the current landing. The airship path caps the value at seven before dispatch.
Probe above the player and cache the contact code. Read up and down from the joystick action byte and move vertically by two pixels on the corresponding permitted path.
Immediate value saved from the tile probe at $A1BA. Class five inhibits the upward step, and class $12 suppresses the airship lateral exit into $9FB6.
After five climbing updates, test right or left and set the corresponding facing. The stage and the cached overhead classification decide whether to take the exit through $9FB6.
Toggle a one-bit frame index, probe the tile at offset (8,16) and choose either the $0A or $19 base pose before adding the frame index.
Immediate byte carrying the alternating phase of the climbing animation.
Leave pose $0E alone, otherwise increment the timer at $7BAA, use pose 8 below $80 and pose 9 thereafter, and reset the timer on reaching $A0.
Select pose $0A, reset the action counter and choose movement mode three.
Select pose $19 and enter the common climbing-state setup.
Leave a pending transition intact. In the temple set the transition byte to $80. In other stages set it to one and adjust the current movement mode for the loss sequence.
Use pose $0D outside the temple and proceed to the pose-change check.
Move two pixels right and four down, set pose $0E and wait four updates before testing the landing tile.
With A holding the horizontal probe offset, sample at Y offset $26. Classes zero and six keep the player in falling mode, while other classes restore movement mode zero.
An RTS follows the tail jump at $A338 and precedes the action branch target at $A33C.
Add A to world X and field-relative X. Past the right field threshold, transfer the increment to the camera unless the horizontal scroll limit is already reached.
High-byte threshold tested before checking the low byte of the maximum horizontal camera coordinate.
Low-byte threshold tested after the high camera coordinate reaches six. Continuing player motion at the boundary advances the field-relative position rather than the scroll coordinate.
Subtract A from world X and field-relative X. Crossing the left threshold can subtract the same amount from horizontal scroll while the camera has room to move.
Begin the upward motion path by subtracting A from the player's two-byte world Y.
Add A to world Y and field-relative Y, then transfer the increment to the camera when the lower field threshold and scroll limit permit it.
Patched high-byte limit for vertical camera motion. Below this boundary the branch at $A52E takes the path that advances the scroll position.
Immediate comparison operand for the vertical camera boundary. At or beyond the boundary the routine accumulates the movement at $7A64, otherwise it adds the step to the scroll position.

Take a horizontal offset in A and vertical offset in Y, convert the resulting world-space point into a tile coordinate and fetch the corresponding map character through $3400/$3500. Train and temple have specific return paths.
This store formats the low three bits of player Y as a digit. It also overwrites the two-bit reversal entry for input $6C because $0754 is inside the table at $06E8.
This store formats the low three bits of player X as a digit. It also overwrites the two-bit reversal entry for input $6E at $0756.
Patched initial map probe page. $A5EB saves it to the scratch pointer high byte ahead of the selected row lookup.
Immediate low byte first loaded into the scratch tile pointer before the selected row's pointer replaces it.
Patched tile column loaded into Y immediately before the tail jump to $A621.
Compare the saved horizontal offset with $10. For smaller offsets decrement the 16-bit map pointer before fetching the next tile. The entry path into this block remains open.
Horizontal offset saved at $A592. The neighbour-selection comparison at $A609 uses it to select the direction.
Increment the low pointer byte and carry to the high byte on wrap. Then fall through to the tile fetch at $A621.
Read the character through the saved map pointer using column Y, then use the character code or its stage-specific classification as the caller's result.
Read the class byte for the tile in Y. The selected stage patches the operand so each loaded charset can give the same glyph index different contact semantics.

The store at $AEED patches the low byte of the contact lookup to $00 in the caves, catacombs, airship and temple states, and to $96 in the train state. The train tile probe takes the separate branch at $A627.
High byte of the indexed contact lookup at $A64F. The stage setup store at $AEE7 writes $31, $00, $32, $33 or $00 for the caves, train, catacombs, airship and temple respectively.
Read the original map column from the patched LDY operand. Clear this cell and its neighbour in two successive map rows before dispatching the contact reward.
Immediate column saved by $A64A for the item handler. The code clears the item’s two-by-two tile image and dispatches using its collision class.
Add 25 to the score, reset the two cave light counters and reinstall the stage palette.
Replace nine ten-cell strips and write the pair $1C/$1D in three other map rows.
Write the four player-layer sprite indices into both screen buffers. OR the current group selector at $7A57 into each base pointer.
Convert Indy’s world X to screen X by subtracting the camera position and adding $20. All four layers share the low byte and the high-bit mask. The routine saves the screen coordinate for tile tests.
Subtract the low camera Y from Indy’s world Y and add $37. Put the leg layers 21 pixels below the upper layers, then adjust both pairs for selected poses or the alternate room state.
Immediate scanline offset added at $A81D when converting from viewport-relative Y to VIC sprite Y.
Offset copied from the selected pose's correction at $A864 and then added to the lower sprite pair.
Save the requested effect byte and advance a modulo-eight counter. Queue the saved effect on phase zero.
Immediate modulo-eight phase incremented before deciding whether to queue the saved effect.
Effect number saved at the start of the periodic sound routine, used on its active phase.
For stage zero or one, choose the map column and row pitch. Fill eight vertically adjacent cells with the tile in A, or with the stage-specific default when A is zero.
Low byte of the addition that advances the fill pointer by one map row. It comes from the active stage’s stride table.
High byte paired with $A8DF for the next-row addition.
Starting address high bytes for the cave and catacombs column writer.
Starting address low bytes for the cave and catacombs column writer.
Default glyphs substituted when the requested column tile is zero.
Tail-jump into the train's scripted-movement entry when a train movement handler detects the fire bit.
Check fire first, then examine the right-hand train contact code in train position state three. Handle blocked or special tiles before the normal two-pixel right step.
Check fire first. In train position state zero, require a nonzero train position byte and examine the left tile before the normal two-pixel step.
Request a life-loss transition and change Indy’s sprite pose to $0D.

Increment the counter in this instruction's operand. On the second hit reset it and set $7AAF, which makes the foreground branch to $8EB4. In both cases write $7F to $816B, $1B to $40F7 and $40F8, and $11 to $41F7 and $F1F8.
Initial counter byte of the LDA at $A96C. The code at $A96E through $A997 updates it, changes $7AAF at two and replaces four absolute bytes before returning. Room setup clears the counter at $AD82.

Subtract one from a two-part substep counter and move up and left by two pixels. At substep zero dispatch selected probe codes before moving. The $99 case delegates to $A96C, $81 enters $A961, $82 returns and $83 skips the handler at $AB08.
Add one to a two-part substep counter and move down and right by two pixels. When the low counter is three, probe the map first. The full counter at $AB03 stops this path when it reaches five.
Current row in the train collision map. The collision fetch uses it to select a map row base.
Temporary vertical destination row tested and updated by the train movement path.
Current column in the train collision map. Neighbour probes temporarily offset it before fetching a tile.
Horizontal phase within the current train column. It wraps modulo four and adjusts the column at each wrap.
Vertical phase used by the train alignment and movement paths. The aligner restores it to eight.
Pass the current phase minus eight to the downward movement routine when the phase differs from eight, then store eight as the new phase.
Add one modulo four to the sub-tile X phase, incrementing the column at $AB05 on wrap to zero.
Subtract one modulo four from the sub-tile X phase, decrementing the column on wrap to three.
Temporarily add three to the train column index, fetch the current row's tile and restore the original column.
At a nonzero current column, temporarily increment it to read an adjacent tile. At column zero increment the border register and return $82 directly.
Read two columns ahead and one row above when the row is nonzero. At the top row read on that same row. Restore the row and column after the fetch.
Test the cell two columns ahead and one row below. On row five, read on the current row. Restore the original indices after reading.
Take the current row selector from $AB03, fetch its 16-bit base through $ABD8/$ABDF and read the cell at column $AB05.
Queue movement effect $10 on the periodic clock, advance the shared phase and increment the pose modulo eight on every second call.
High bytes of seven 256-byte map row bases beginning at $4500.
Low bytes of the same map rows, all zero.
Player probe state written at $A7F0 and tested on the three tile scan paths at $9EDF, $9F54 and $9FC8.
Companion player probe state written at $A80C and tested on the three tile scan paths at $9ED8, $9F4D and $9FBB.

Replace tile codes $98–$A1 with blank cells across 63 map pages beginning at $3600. Clear the four animation pointers and restore the six-cell patterns for ten map positions from the paired pointer tables at $B634 and $B63E.
Branch selector for the alternate room setup. When zero, increment the selector and set the persistent room flag before using the stage table.
Alternate room screen selector. The renderer and foreground loop test it, and room setup clears it at $AC7D.
Preserve the room index across disk loading, ensure the required asset set is resident, and initialize room state from the stage descriptor table through $B1D0.
Write 256 split row pointers from a base of $3600 into $3400 and $3500. Add the stage stride from $B19D and $B1A1 between adjacent pointers.
Use a stage-selected glyph to fill the shared playfield rows at $0400 and $0C00 and initialize colour RAM before drawing the room.
Tile value chosen during stage setup to fill the two field buffers before rendering.
Set the room flags and player defaults, clear pending actions and build both sprite buffers. Initialize the display and per-room counters before entering play.
Immediate byte of CPX at $AFED. The riddle chooses a value from one through five and compares it with X to save the matching generated word index. The exit also uses it at $9FF2.
Immediate countdown restored into X after writing three display glyphs for the generated word. Once all six are drawn, use the saved index and threshold tables to make the clue.
Mix the raster line and VIC control value into the software counters at $7D2E/$7D2F. Return the generated pair in $FE/$FF for the threshold chooser.
Offsets selecting the first record of the stage-specific map setup patches at $B0F4.

Stage-indexed records used by $AF00. The first byte is the tile ID. The pointer bytes at record offsets two and three give a target with a fixed $0A00 bias. Zero as the first byte terminates the sequence.
Stage-indexed sprite indices copied to $7C10.
Stage-indexed sprite indices copied to $7C11.
Initial colour of the first panel sprite for each stage before timer and hazard updates.
Stage-indexed blank glyphs used by transition fill and the scroll renderer. The train subsection substitutes glyph $02.
Stage-specific value patched into the VIC first multicolour background load at $81DF.
Stage-specific second multicolour background value patched into the operand at $81E1.
Three high bytes used to patch the contact table operand at $A651. They select $3100, $3200 and $3300.
Low bytes paired with $B197. The three pages are aligned at offset zero.
Low bytes of the map row stride for the four main stage indices. The catacombs use 150 bytes per row and the other indices use 256.
High bytes of the map row stride, paired with $B19D by the pointer-building loop at $AD03.
Stage-indexed low byte of the right camera boundary, copied into the comparison at $A3D4.
Stage-indexed high byte of the right camera boundary, copied into the comparison at $A3CD.
Stage-indexed low byte of the vertical camera boundary, copied into the comparison at $A534.
Stage-indexed high byte of the vertical camera boundary, copied into the comparison at $A52D.
Initial VIC Y offset installed for the player's field sprites. The train replaces it with $2D.
Source high bytes used by $B7DC when copying a stage's character-to-colour table. The train is the fifth selector.
Low bytes paired with $B1B9. Adding $80 gives the base of the second half of the source table.
Byte offsets into the working room descriptor page at $2700, in steps of 20. Indexed by the room selector at $ACA5.
Four little-endian pointers to the per-stage room descriptor collections. $AC8A selects one using twice the stage index.
High bytes of the four interleaved room table pointers. Each pointer selects a page to copy into working RAM.

Nine 20-byte records for the first stage. In each record, the first four little-endian values supply player world X/Y and camera scroll X/Y. Offsets $08–$0A initialize field-relative position and $12 selects the subsection.
Five 20-byte room records addressed by the stage-index-one pointer in $B1D0. Room setup uses the same record stride as the first stage.
Five 20-byte room descriptors for stage index two. The initial record starts with world X=$01E5 and Y=$002F.
Five 20-byte room descriptors for stage index three. The first record starts at X=0, Y=$003E with initial horizontal and vertical camera offsets of zero and six.
Return from the actor scan while the alternate room screen is active.
Skip the alternate room state. Seed the actor and room scans with different ranges for the train subsection and the main cave stage.

Immediate operand of CPX at $B3DA. Skip the active record, then use the remaining enabled room records to find an actor within range of the player. On selection copy the coordinates and type from $2700 and install type-specific graphics state.
Type-indexed initial values copied to $7BEF when a room record becomes active.
Type-indexed initial values copied to $7BF0 when a room record becomes active.
Type-indexed initial values copied into the operand at $8DF8.
Advance to the next actor record and compare the new index with the patched scan limit.
Stop scanning actor records when the incremented index matches this immediate boundary.
Immediate starting index for the room proximity scan. The following comparison skips the current room.

Immediate room index used by the scan. For each candidate, require equal high player coordinates and absolute low-byte differences below 16 horizontally and 40 vertically. Store the index for the first matching room.
Immediate upper limit for the candidate-room proximity loop, patched with the cave or train range.
Clear the VIC display-enable bit and set the panel interrupt's blanking operand to one.
Set bit 4 of the VIC display control value and clear the panel IRQ's blanking operand.
Copy nine ten-tile strips into consecutive map rows at column $3F, then replace the two cells at column $CC in each of three other rows.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $6C00 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $6D00 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $6E00 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $6F00 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $7000 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $7100 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $7200 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $7300 from column $3F.
Ten replacement tiles for row at $7400 from column $3F.
Ten tile values copied into the map row at $6C00 starting at column $3F when the relevant item is collected.
Ten tiles for the corresponding patch at $6D3F.
Ten tiles for the corresponding patch at $6E3F.
Ten tiles for the corresponding patch at $6F3F.
Ten tiles for the corresponding patch at $703F.
Ten blank tiles written at $713F.
Alternating $56/$57 tile pairs written beginning at $723F.
